notes.title: The logistic quarter-turn
notes.summary: A two-cycle has return multiplier −1 at r = 1 + √6. Its paired derivative matrix has fourth power I, and the fourth-return displacement has zero first derivative at the cycle points.
notes.nextStep: Read the companion cubic calculation to obtain local attraction and its rate. For a further geometric connection, specify the state space, map and quantity to compare with its defined invariant-circle model.

notes.title: Alternating real towers
notes.summary: For every real base c > 1, the alternating-sign system has one pair of phases. The explicit iteration converges from every upper starting phase at least 1, with a uniform contraction bound.
notes.nextStep: Compare the convergence and inverse classification with the literature. If a particular arithmetic constant is used as a target height, state the additional arithmetic question separately.

notes.title: A dyadic vanishing remainder
notes.summary: The lacunary series f(x) = Σ x^(2^n), where 2^n means 2 raised to n, obeys f(x) = x + f(x²). Along the specified dyadic path toward 1, subtracting k and a convergent constant leaves an explicit tail.
notes.nextStep: Quantify the finite-k relative error beyond the proved leading-ratio limit, or define a structural map and the property it preserves. A shared dynamical system or conjugacy remains open.

notes.title: Prime polynomials count exactly
notes.summary: Finite polynomial products encode ordered Goldbach representations and twin-prime translations. A diagonal correction converts ordered Goldbach counts into unordered counts.

notes.title: The Z(p) family under Schanuel
notes.summary: Euler’s even-zeta formula gives exact rational coefficients cₚ for every odd integer p ≥ 3. Assuming complex Schanuel, π and any finite list of the corresponding Z(p) values are algebraically independent.
notes.nextStep: Compare this specific conditional consequence with the literature. State any proposed unconditional result as a separate claim with its own assumptions.

notes.title: Two constructions of six
notes.summary: The additive and multiplicative constructions of six define different fractional exponential maps. Their smooth-branch derivatives give exact finite-time Lyapunov averages in terms of separate orbit means.
notes.nextStep: Define the orbit or invariant measure of interest and establish the limiting means before evaluating a zero-difference target. Keep the two maps’ means separate.

notes.title: Palindrome counting
notes.statusLabel: Exact count under a sampling model
notes.summary: For independent uniform q-symbol strings of length n, ordinary palindromes have probability q^(−floor(n/2)). The example q = 4, n = 40 has probability exactly 2^(−40).
notes.nextStep: Before making a biophysical claim, specify a physical alphabet, pairing rule and measurable stability or decay criterion. The finite combinatorics supplies no biochemical feasibility result.

notes.title: Dimensions and recovered fragments
notes.summary: Products, tensor products and changes of scalar field give different dimensions. Equal continuum cardinalities do not identify those dimensions, fractal dimensions or physical degrees of freedom.
notes.nextStep: Recover explicit definitions of T₀–T₃ and the intended connecting map. State which structure is preserved before comparing dimensions, dynamics or geometric collapse.

notes.title: Review of the written proofs
notes.summary: The logistic, alternating-tower and finite prime-counting arguments establish the stated identities, bounds and classifications. This note identifies their key proof steps and source versions.

notes.statusLabel: Proved local attraction; physical interpretation open
notes.summary: The restoring logistic cubic proves local attraction with an inverse-square-root error rate. An explicitly defined product model transfers that result to transverse attraction toward an invariant circle, and a separate tail estimate proves the dyadic–zeta ratio limit.
